title: Systems of Linear ODEs & Phase Plane Topology

sections.heading: Systems of Linear ODEs & Phase Plane Topology Practice Exercises

questions.q: The matrix of \( \mathbf x'=A\mathbf x \) has eigenvalues \( \pm i \). The origin is a:
questions.answer: Complex eigenvalues give spirals; the sign of the real part decides stability, and a zero real part gives a center. Here: center (stable, not asymptotically).

questions.q: Solve \( x'=2 x,\ y'=- y \) with \( x(0)=-1,\ y(0)=3 \). Find \( x(\ln{\left(2 \right)}) \).
questions.answer: The equations are decoupled: \( x=- e^{2 t} \), \( y=3 e^{- t} \). Hence \( -4 \).

questions.q: With \( x_1=y \), \( x_2=y' \), the equation \( y''+3y=0 \) becomes \( \mathbf x'=A\mathbf x \). Find \( A \).
questions.answer: \( x_1'=x_2 \) and \( x_2'=y''=- 3 x_{1} \), so \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}0 & 1\\-3 & 0\end{matrix}\right] \).

questions.q: The matrix of \( \mathbf x'=A\mathbf x \) has eigenvalues \( \pm 5i \). The origin is a:
questions.answer: Complex eigenvalues give spirals; the sign of the real part decides stability, and a zero real part gives a center. Here: center (stable, not asymptotically).

questions.q: Solve \( x'=- x,\ y'=- y \) with \( x(0)=-2,\ y(0)=4 \). Find \( y(\ln{\left(2 \right)}) \).
questions.answer: The equations are decoupled: \( x=- 2 e^{- t} \), \( y=4 e^{- t} \). Hence \( 2 \).

questions.q: With \( x_1=y \), \( x_2=y' \), the equation \( y''+y'+y=0 \) becomes \( \mathbf x'=A\mathbf x \). Find \( A \).
questions.answer: \( x_1'=x_2 \) and \( x_2'=y''=- x_{1} - x_{2} \), so \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}0 & 1\\-1 & -1\end{matrix}\right] \).

questions.q: The matrix of \( \mathbf x'=A\mathbf x \) has eigenvalues \( -2\pm 4i \). The origin is a:
questions.answer: Complex eigenvalues give spirals; the sign of the real part decides stability, and a zero real part gives a center. Here: stable spiral.
The equations are decoupled: \( x=4 e^{- t} \), \( y=- e^{t} \). Hence \( \frac{4}{e} \).

questions.q: The second-order linear homogeneous ODE \( u''(s) - 40u'(s) + 144u(s) = 0 \) has characteristic roots \( \lambda_1, \lambda_2 \). Determine the trace sum \( \lambda_1 + \lambda_2 \).
questions.answer: From \( \lambda^2 - 40\lambda + 144 = 0 \), the sum of roots is \( 40 \).

questions.q:
Consider the system of linear differential equations given by: \(\qquad \begin{cases} \dfrac{dx}{dt} = -x + 2y \\ \dfrac{dy}{dt} = 3x - 2y \end{cases}\)

Let the general solution be of the form \( \mathbf{x}(t) = c_1 \mathbf{v}_1 e^{\lambda_1 t} + c_2 \mathbf{v}_2 e^{\lambda_2 t} \), where \( \lambda_1 < \lambda_2 \). Determine the value of \( \lambda_2 \).
questions.answer:
The given system can be written in matrix form as \( \dfrac{d\mathbf{x}}{dt} = A\mathbf{x} \), where \( A = \begin{pmatrix} -1 & 2 \\ 3 & -2 \end{pmatrix} \).

To find the eigenvalues \( \lambda \), we solve the characteristic equation \( \det(A - \lambda I) = 0 \).
\( \det \begin{pmatrix} -1-\lambda & 2 \\ 3 & -2-\lambda \end{pmatrix} = 0 \)
\( (-1-\lambda)(-2-\lambda) - (2)(3) = 0 \)
\( (1+\lambda)(2+\lambda) - 6 = 0 \)
\( 2 + \lambda + 2\lambda + \lambda^2 - 6 = 0 \)
\( \lambda^2 + 3\lambda - 4 = 0 \)

Factoring the quadratic equation:
\( (\lambda + 4)(\lambda - 1) = 0 \)

The eigenvalues are \( \lambda_1 = -4 \) and \( \lambda_2 = 1 \).

Since the problem states \( \lambda_1 < \lambda_2 \), we have \( \lambda_1 = -4 \) and \( \lambda_2 = 1 \). The question asks for \( \lambda_2 \).

questions.q: The separable initial value problem \( \dfrac{du}{ds} = 18s \) satisfies \( u(0) = 8 \). Determine the solution value \( u(7) \).
questions.answer: Integrating gives \( u(s) = 9s^2 + 8 \), so \( u(7) = 449 \).

questions.q: Consider the system of linear differential equations: \(\begin{aligned} \frac{dx}{dt} &= ax + by \\ \frac{dy}{dt} &= cx + dy \end{aligned}\) where \(a, b, c, d\) are constants. The characteristic equation for the system is \(\lambda^2 - (a+d)\lambda + (ad-bc) = 0\). We are given that the eigenvalues of the system are \(\lambda_1 = 2\) and \(\lambda_2 = -1\). The trace of the coefficient matrix, \(T = a+d\), is \(1\). Determine the value of the determinant of the coefficient matrix, \(D = ad-bc\).
questions.answer: The characteristic equation of a 2x2 system of linear differential equations \(\begin{aligned} \frac{dx}{dt} &= ax + by \\ \frac{dy}{dt} &= cx + dy \end{aligned}\) is given by \(\lambda^2 - (a+d)\lambda + (ad-bc) = 0\). This can be written in terms of the trace (T = a+d) and determinant (D = ad-bc) of the coefficient matrix as \(\lambda^2 - T\lambda + D = 0\). We are given that the eigenvalues are \(\lambda_1 = 2\) and \(\lambda_2 = -1\). The sum of the roots of a quadratic equation \(p\lambda^2 + q\lambda + r = 0\) is \(-q/p\), and the product of the roots is \(r/p\). For the characteristic equation \(\lambda^2 - T\lambda + D = 0\), the sum of the eigenvalues is \(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2 = -(-T)/1 = T\), and the product of the eigenvalues is \(\lambda_1 \lambda_2 = D/1 = D\). We are given that the trace \(T = a+d = 1\). Let's verify this with the given eigenvalues: \(\lambda_1 + \lambda_2 = 2 + (-1) = 1\), which matches the given trace. We need to find the determinant \(D = ad-bc\). Using the product of the eigenvalues: \(D = \lambda_1 \lambda_2 = (2)(-1) = -2\).

questions.q:
Consider the system of linear differential equations given by:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac{dx}{dt} &= x + 2y \\
\frac{dy}{dt} &= 3x + 2y
\end{aligned}
\]
If the solution to this system is of the form \(x(t) = c_1 e^{\lambda_1 t} + c_2 e^{\lambda_2 t}\) and \(y(t) = k_1 c_1 e^{\lambda_1 t} + k_2 c_2 e^{\lambda_2 t}\), what is the value of the larger eigenvalue \(\lambda\)?
questions.answer:
The given system can be written in matrix form as \(\mathbf{x}'(t) = A \mathbf{x}(t)\), where \(A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\) and \(\mathbf{x}(t) = \begin{pmatrix} x(t) \\ y(t) \end{pmatrix}\).
To find the eigenvalues \(\lambda\), we solve the characteristic equation \(\det(A - \lambda I) = 0\), where \(I\) is the identity matrix.

\(\det \begin{pmatrix} 1-\lambda & 2 \\ 3 & 2-\lambda \end{pmatrix} = 0\)

\((1-\lambda)(2-\lambda) - (2)(3) = 0\)

\(2 - \lambda - 2\lambda + \lambda^2 - 6 = 0\)

\(\lambda^2 - 3\lambda - 4 = 0\)

Factoring the quadratic equation:

\((\lambda - 4)(\lambda + 1) = 0\)

The eigenvalues are \(\lambda_1 = 4\) and \(\lambda_2 = -1\). The larger eigenvalue is 4.

questions.q: With \( x_1=y \), \( x_2=y' \), the equation \( y''+3y'-4y=0 \) becomes \( \mathbf x'=A\mathbf x \). Find \( A \).
questions.answer: \( x_1'=x_2 \) and \( x_2'=y''=4 x_{1} - 3 x_{2} \), so \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}0 & 1\\4 & -3\end{matrix}\right] \).

questions.q: The matrix of \( \mathbf x'=A\mathbf x \) has eigenvalues -5 and 3. The origin is a:
questions.answer: Real eigenvalues of opposite sign give a saddle; same sign gives a node (stable if negative). Here: saddle point (unstable).
The equations are decoupled: \( x=3 e^{t} \), \( y=- 2 e^{2 t} \). Hence \( 3 e^{2} \).

questions.q: With \( x_1=y \), \( x_2=y' \), the equation \( y''-5y'+y=0 \) becomes \( \mathbf x'=A\mathbf x \). Find \( A \).
questions.answer: \( x_1'=x_2 \) and \( x_2'=y''=- x_{1} + 5 x_{2} \), so \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}0 & 1\\-1 & 5\end{matrix}\right] \).

questions.q: In this problem, the matrix of \( \mathbf x'=A\mathbf x \) has eigenvalues -3 and 2. The origin is a:
questions.answer: Real eigenvalues of opposite sign give a saddle; same sign gives a node (stable if negative). Here: saddle point (unstable).
The equations are decoupled: \( x=- e^{3 t} \), \( y=4 e^{t} \). Hence \( - e^{3} \).

questions.q: With \( x_1=y \), \( x_2=y' \), the equation \( y''+2y=0 \) becomes \( \mathbf x'=A\mathbf x \). Find \( A \).
questions.answer: \( x_1'=x_2 \) and \( x_2'=y''=- 2 x_{1} \), so \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}0 & 1\\-2 & 0\end{matrix}\right] \).

questions.q: In this problem, the matrix of \( \mathbf x'=A\mathbf x \) has eigenvalues \( \pm 4i \). The origin is a:
questions.answer: Complex eigenvalues give spirals; the sign of the real part decides stability, and a zero real part gives a center. Here: center (stable, not asymptotically).

questions.q: With \( x_1=y \), \( x_2=y' \), the equation \( y''-3y'-2y=0 \) becomes \( \mathbf x'=A\mathbf x \). Find \( A \).
questions.answer: \( x_1'=x_2 \) and \( x_2'=y''=2 x_{1} + 3 x_{2} \), so \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}0 & 1\\2 & 3\end{matrix}\right] \).

questions.q: The matrix of \( \mathbf x'=A\mathbf x \) has eigenvalues 3 and -4. The origin is a:
questions.answer: Real eigenvalues of opposite sign give a saddle; same sign gives a node (stable if negative). Here: saddle point (unstable).
The equations are decoupled: \( x=- 2 e^{- 2 t} \), \( y=- 2 e^{- 3 t} \). Hence \( - \frac{2}{e^{6}} \).

questions.q: With \( x_1=y \), \( x_2=y' \), the equation \( y''+4y'+3y=0 \) becomes \( \mathbf x'=A\mathbf x \). Find \( A \).
questions.answer: \( x_1'=x_2 \) and \( x_2'=y''=- 3 x_{1} - 4 x_{2} \), so \( A=\left[\begin{matrix}0 & 1\\-3 & -4\end{matrix}\right] \).
